name: Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Painful Fissures

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse thickening and hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles
Painful fissuring and cracking of the palmoplantar skin
Onset of symptoms in infancy or early childhood
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histopathological confirmation showing epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with painful fissures plus either early onset or supportive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse thickening and hyperkeratosis of palms and soles
searchTerms: widespread thickening and scaling of palms and soles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painful fissures and cracks in palmoplantar skin
searchTerms: painful skin cracks on palms and soles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetrical involvement of both palms and soles
searchTerms: both hands and feet affected symmetrically
equal involvement of palms and soles
pain worsened by pressure or use
pain triggered by touching or movement
excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet
nail changes linked to thickened skin

occasional.symptomName: Mild fissuring extending beyond palmoplantar surfaces
searchTerms: mild skin cracking beyond palms and soles
skin splits spreading past palmoplantar areas
psoriasis-like plaques outside hands and feet
scaly red patches beyond palmoplantar regions
mild hearing loss from nerve damage

blistering on hyperkeratotic palms and soles

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia and compact orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Negative fungal cultures unless secondary infection present
other: Clinical examination revealing diffuse thickening and fissuring of palms and soles
Pain assessment correlating with fissure severity

distinguishingFeatures: Nail dystrophy more prominent and early
Genetic mutations in KRT6, KRT16, or KRT17 genes

redFlags: Severe painful fissures impairing hand and foot function
Signs of secondary bacterial or fungal infection
Rapid progression or involvement beyond palms and soles
references: Smith FJ et al. Keratin mutations in diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma. J Invest Dermatol. 2002.
